key_insight: Region-reducing ReLU neural networks by stabilizing unstable neurons and merging redundant ones can cut the number of linear regions, improving optimization performance without sacrificing prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For optimization-heavy engineering applications such as chemical process superstructure design, this compression strategy can substantially reduce solve time and produce near-reference solutions at lower computational cost.
method: Stabilize unstable neurons to simplify the ReLU activation geometry.
Merge redundant neurons to reduce the number of linear regions on the domain of interest.
Use error compensation to preserve predictive accuracy after compression.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate the approach on the 2D peaks function, three chemical-process surrogate models, and a hybrid superstructure optimization problem, reporting about 40%–50% faster computation and solutions within 1% of the reference for the superstructure case.
watch_item: The method is geometry-aware and problem-dependent, so its benefit may vary with network architecture, training quality, and the specific optimization domain.
paper_title: Optimization with Region-Reduced ReLU Neural Networks
